title: Pay Your Attention on Lib! Android Third-Party Library Detection via Feature Language Model
venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering (SANER)
detection_method: Pre-train Transformer on 200M Smali tokens from AndroZoo → fine-tune binary classifier using SDK structural vocabulary (reserved types, structural symbols); data compression via pre-trained model properties
module_decoupling: None — operates on entire decompiled Smali code as token sequence; detects library presence/absence without locating library boundaries
features_used: SDK structural vocabulary (reserved types, structural symbols)
Transformer attention patterns over Smali sequences
matching_algorithm: Binary classification via fine-tuned Transformer; predicts presence/absence of a specific library based on learned representations of Smali token sequences
obfuscation_handling: Learns obfuscation patterns from data during pre-training — handles RN (renaming), PF (package flattening), CFR (control-flow randomization), DCR (dead code removal), SE (string encryption), MI (method inlining); most R8-resilient approach evaluated
r8_resilience: +30% F1 over rule-based tools on R8-obfuscated dataset (most R8-resilient approach as of 2025)
lib_level_f1: ~39% F1 on non-obfuscated apps (below top rule-based tools); R8-resilient F1 higher but exact number not specified (+30% relative improvement)
version_level_f1: None — binary presence/absence only, no version identification
precision: Not explicitly reported as standalone metric
recall: Not explicitly reported as standalone metric
speed: ~472s per app (AndroGuard Smali decompilation dominates processing time; model inference is fast)
dataset_size: 200M Smali tokens from AndroZoo for pre-training; 10,000 real apps for evaluation (found 28 vulnerable TPLs appearing 42,408 times)
partial_lib_handling: Binary detection only (present/absent per library); no partial inclusion scoring
sbom_output: No — cannot produce SBOM since it lacks version identification entirely
open_source: Code described in paper but full release unclear as of 2025
cve_mapping: No automated CVE mapping demonstrated (manual analysis of 28 vulnerable TPLs found in evaluation)
transitive_deps: No — binary classifier does not model dependency relationships
strengths: Most R8-resilient approach evaluated (+30% F1 over rule-based on R8 datasets)
Learns obfuscation patterns from data (handles 6 obfuscation types: RN, PF, CFR, DCR, SE, MI)
Pre-training on 200M Smali tokens reduces need for labeled training data
Transformer architecture captures long-range structural dependencies in Smali
Useful for first-pass filtering / library presence screening at scale
weaknesses: Binary presence/absence detection only — NO version identification, cannot produce SBOMs or map CVEs by version
Weak on non-obfuscated apps (~39% F1, below top rule-based tools)
~472s per app is slow (AndroGuard preprocessing bottleneck)
Cannot locate library boundaries within app code (no module decoupling)
impact_on_project: LibAttention represents the cutting edge for R8-resilient detection but is fundamentally insufficient for SBOM generation due to the complete absence of version identification. The approach is valuable as a potential first-pass filter in a multi-stage pipeline — use LibAttention to detect which libraries are present (especially in R8-obfuscated apps), then apply a version-identification method on the detected subset. The pre-training approach (200M Smali tokens from AndroZoo) reduces the labeled data burden, which could be leveraged for a version-capable model. However, the Transformer-based architecture must be extended with version-level classification heads or combined with a structural matching approach to enable SBOM production.
